messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/timeouts detected for Private VPC customers in eu-west-1. Affected service: inference-gateway-egress. Pager: https://pager.redwood/INC-2158765432 :rotating_light:
ryan.c: Acked. Oncall here. Seeing a spike in 504/502 from the edge -> inference-gateway. Traffic looks normal upstream but we have high connection resets. Pushing to network team.
elaine.p: jumping in. Which AZs? any peering changes or recent firewall rollouts?
maria.g: Logs show large number of downstream connections timing out when calling 10.0.3.4:443 (egress gateway). Sample from gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:21Z] conn_id=abc123 upstream=10.0.3.4:443 status=504 proto=TFO reason=conn_reset
[2026-03-15T10:12:22Z] conn_id=def456 upstream=10.0.3.4:443 status=200 proto=TLS
[2026-03-15T10:12:23Z] conn_id=ghi789 upstream=10.0.3.4:443 status=502 proto=RST
```
devon.p: NAT metrics show ephemeral port pool at 99% for the transit NAT appliance in eu-west-1a. Cloud metrics: nat_allocation_failures spiked.
elaine.p: that points to SNAT port exhaustion or conntrack table full. Can we get conntrack / iptables errors from the NAT instances?
maria.g: grabbed dmesg from NAT instance: 
```
conntrack: table full, dropping packet
ipv4: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping
```
priya.s: customer impact: initial estimate ~14% of Private customers in eu-west experiencing timeouts for model inference calls. Several support tickets from Samir.cs show client retries and increased latency.
samir.cs: Confirming. Two enterprise customers reported 5xx errors from our hosted endpoint starting ~10:11Z. They are on private peering with egress through our shared NAT.
ryan.c: Okay, triage path: 1) validate if NACL/SG changes caused this, 2) check nat appliance conntrack table and port usage, 3) short-term mitigation: route affected subnets to alternative NAT or add ephemeral port capacity.
elaine.p: I checked infra audit log -> no recent NACL or SG changes in last 24h for the peering subnets. Peering attachment flaps are visible: transit-gw reported peering keepalive retries around 10:09-10:12Z. Could be transient ballooning that caused connection churn and conntrack exhaustion.
devon.p: I'm provisioning a new NAT instance with higher ephemeral allocation and scaling conntrack limits. Running command to bump nf_conntrack max: 
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=180
```
ryan.c: Good. Also please add a second NAT in eu-west-1b and update route table for affected private peering route to a higher-capacity target.
devon.p: Starting that now, ETA ~6 mins. I'll also add a temporary route to a dedicated egress pool for Private customers to drain connections.
maria.g: Adding short-lived mitigation: enable aggressive connection TTL reduction on gateways to free conntrack entries quicker. Patch rolling to inference-gateway fleet.
elaine.p: I'm seeing BGP flaps between our transit and partner peering at 10:08Z. That matches churn we saw on the gateway. I'll open a peering ticket with our carrier and set up a route to avoid the flapped path.
incident-bot: incident updated. Severity set to SEV2 due to customer impact and multiple enterprise customers affected.
priya.s: Communication: I'll draft a brief status for CSE and customers. Key points: acknowledging elevated 5xx, active mitigation (scaling NAT, route changes), ETA for mitigation ~20-30 mins.
samir.cs: Please include that this is isolated to Private VPC peering egress in eu-west-1; public hosted API unaffected. Customers want to know if data left region.\y r an.c: (typo) ignore
ryan.c: note: public endpoints are fine, this is egress from Private peering through shared NAT. No evidence of data exfil or model quality impact.
maria.g: NAT instance now shows conntrack table usage dropping after sysctl change and additional NAT up: 
```
Before: nf_conntrack_count=1985000 nf_conntrack_max=2000000
After: nf_conntrack_count=45000 nf_conntrack_max=2000000
```
devon.p: New NAT up and route updated for affected peering attachments. I'm seeing 5xx rates drop back toward baseline.\elaine.p: Can we throttle client connections temporarily? Add a denylist for noisy source IPs from the peered ranges?\ryan.c: We can apply a rate-limiting rule at the ingress to the inference-gateway but let's avoid breaking legitimate traffic. Prefer routing to dedicated egress pool.
priya.s: Draft status posted to customers channel and flagged to account teams.
incident-bot: Paging escalation: handoff to maria.g for full RCA and ticket creation in infra backlog (TICKET-8342). Next steps: detailed postmortem, build automated conntrack alerts, and consider dedicated NAT per-customer for high-throughput private peers.
maria.g: I'll own RCA. Initial hypothesis: peering flaps caused connection churn which pushed NAT conntrack and ephemeral port allocation to exhaustion; this led to upstream 5xx/timeouts. Need to verify if any retransmit storm from client side amplified this.
samir.cs: Running list of affected customers attached to the incident doc. Adding their owners for follow-up.
priya.s: ETA for full RCA doc and follow-up runbook changes: EOD today for immediate remediation plan, full postmortem by EOW.
elaine.p: Action items assigned: 
- maria.g: RCA and postmortem (TICKET-8342)
- devon.p: permanent NAT autoscaling + conntrack tuning + monitoring (TICKET-8343)
- ry an.c: add runbook steps for peering flaps and emergency egress reroute (TICKET-8344)
- priya.s/samir.cs: customer comms and bridge with account teams (TICKET-8345)
ryan.c: Thanks team. Keeping this thread open for final confirmation. If 5xx resurges, page SRE again. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident 'INC-2158765432' acknowledged and assigned. Handoff complete.
